trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out around the edge to (1,3) or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: around the edge to (1,3).
Going down, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,4). So the line goes right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,1); going around the edge to (5,4), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (around the edge to (1,3) from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go right.
Going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5); going right, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,3). So the line goes around the edge to (1,4).
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,1). So the line goes left.
Going around the edge to (5,2) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going around the edge to (2,5) would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4). So the line goes right.
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
The line must go right: left is number 10, which comes later.
Going right, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5). So the line goes up.
Cell (2,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going down would strand number 8: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (5,5).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!

Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 72 futures: 96% survive going right (best covers 44%); around the edge to (1,3) 88%; left 0%.
Tried 72 futures: 12% survive going around the edge to (1,4) (best covers 36%); up 0%; right 0%.
Jackpot! A future after going left covers the whole board. Cashing in!
